sections.h2: North Little Rock at a glance
sections.html:
North Little Rock is its own city in Pulaski County, on the north bank of the Arkansas River across from Little Rock. The 2025 estimate is 65,120 residents, up from 64,591 in 2020, and the count has stayed in a narrow range for decades. The 2020 census listed 32,856 housing units, 11.8% of them vacant, so a seller here may compete with a fair number of empty houses and rentals.

Railroads, health care, sports venues and shopping anchor the economy. Baptist Health Medical Center, Simmons Bank Arena, Dickey-Stephens Park, McCain Mall and Lakewood Village are all in the city, and the city sits directly across the river from downtown Little Rock, so employers on both banks are within reach of most streets.

The city includes the Argenta Historic District, Park Hill, Lakewood and Levy, plus Amboy, Arrowhead Manor, Baring Cross, Chimney Rock, Crystal Hill, Dark Hollow, Dixie, Indian Hills, Mid-City, Overbrook, Pike View, Rose City and Windsor Valley. Each area has its own housing age and price pattern, and buyers look at the street before they look at the city. Owners in Park Hill or Argenta have historic standards to think about for exterior work. In Amboy or Indian Hills, storm history is the main talking point.

The EF3 tornado of March 31, 2023, came through North Little Rock after starting in west Little Rock. It passed through Burns Park, Amboy and Indian Hills on its way to Sherwood and Jacksonville, with peak winds of 165 mph. At least 10,000 trees were lost in Burns Park, and across its whole path at least 2,700 structures were affected.

If your house had storm repairs, keep receipts, permits and insurance paperwork together in one folder. Buyers and lenders both ask for them, and a missing permit can hold up a closing.

Owners in the Argenta Historic District need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Historic District Commission before they change a building's exterior. Regulated work includes room additions, doors, windows, awnings, porches and signs, and new construction and demolition also need review.

StepWhat happens
Commission meetingSecond Thursday of each month at 6 p.m.
Public noticePublished two weeks before review, with adjacent owners notified
After approvalBuilding permit from the city planning department, with no permit fee inside the district
If deniedAppeal to the Pulaski County Circuit Court
Commission office506 Main Street, 501-371-0755

Historic rules affect exterior work, not the act of selling. A buyer will still want to know about approved or pending changes, so finish or disclose anything open before closing.

The city council can condemn a nuisance structure by resolution after a public hearing, and it is unlawful to own or maintain a structure once it is condemned. The resolution must describe the structures, name the owners and find them unfit for occupancy or harmful to life, property or public safety.

A nuisance structure can be dilapidated and unsafe, unsanitary enough to threaten health, or a more than ordinary fire hazard. Unsafe structures include those at risk of partial or complete collapse. City Hall is at 300 Main Street and City Services is at 700 W 29th Street, both open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Call City Hall about any specific notice.

If a notice seems likely, a sale before it arrives can spare you the cost of demolition or major repairs.

Interstate 30 ends in North Little Rock, the Arkansas portion of Interstate 57 starts here, and Interstate 40, US 65, US 67 and US 167 pass through. Rock Region Metro runs streetcars through Argenta, and North Little Rock Municipal Airport serves as a reliever for Clinton National. Most students attend the North Little Rock School District, which has one high school, one middle school, nine elementary schools and an early childhood center. The Pulaski County Special School District runs other area schools.

A North Little Rock deed is recorded with the Pulaski Circuit and County Clerk at 401 West Markham Street in Little Rock. Recording costs $15 for the first page and $5 for each added page, and the filing needs a transfer tax form. People filing a deed need a photo ID unless they are attorneys, brokers, financial institution representatives or government representatives. The state's real property transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Arkansas counties collect property tax from the first business day of March through October 15 of the following year, with a 10 percent penalty on late payments. A homestead's taxable value can rise no more than 5 percent a year. To appeal a valuation formally, schedule a hearing with the county board of equalization by the third Monday in August.

Back tax is paid from your proceeds at closing. Get the balance from the county while you compare offers, so you know what you would actually receive.

You can list, sell on your own or accept a cash offer. A cash buyer who takes the house as is can be a fit for storm-damaged, inherited, vacant or tenant-occupied property, especially if a nuisance notice is on the horizon. A cash sale has no lender appraisal, so the closing date depends mostly on how fast the title company clears ownership and liens.

Bring the deed, a photo ID, your latest tax statement and any permit or storm-repair records to the first conversation. For a rental, add the lease. For an inherited house, add the paperwork showing who may sign.

faqs.q: What is North Little Rock's population?
faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 65,120 residents, after 64,591 were counted in 2020.

faqs.q: Do historic district rules affect selling in Argenta?
faqs.a: They affect exterior work, not the act of selling. Owners need a Certificate of Appropriateness for changes like windows, doors, porches and additions, and buyers will ask about open approvals.

faqs.q: Was North Little Rock hit by the 2023 tornado?
faqs.a: Yes. The March 31, 2023 EF3 tornado passed through Burns Park, Amboy and Indian Hills, and at least 10,000 trees were lost in Burns Park.

faqs.q: Can North Little Rock condemn my house?
faqs.a: Yes. The city council can condemn a nuisance structure by resolution after a public hearing, if it finds the building unfit for occupancy or harmful to public safety.

faqs.q: What is the state transfer tax on a deed?
faqs.a: It is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on deeds over $100.
